correctness.rationale: Rebuilt incidence-basis convolution coordinates: diagonal zero products, local a0 u_i + x_i b_i=0, a_i v_i+y_i b∞=0, and top a0 w+z b∞+Σ_i x_i v_i=0. When (a0,b∞) not both zero, top equation has q free (z,w) choices, yielding 2q²(q-1)G10^m+q(q-1)^2 G11^m, with G10=q²(q²+q-1), G11=q²(2q-1). For endpoints both zero, finite-field additive-character orthogonality gives q³[G00^m+(q-1)H^m] where G00=q³(3q-2) and H=q³(2q-1). All four bases are positive/distinct for q>=2, nonzero coefficients and Vandermonde force minimal order four; largest B1 dominates. Checked ordered one-sided vs two-sided conventions, m=0 (two-point chain), m=1 (full triangular 3x3), extension-field char2. Independent exhaustive left-multiplication rank count verified q=2,m=0..3; q=3,m=0..2; q=5,m=0. Source verifier additionally handles genuine F4 and fourteen small cases. These finite counts corroborate the full Fourier argument.

value.rationale: Exact one-sided zero-product counts for an incidence-algebra family with nontrivial composable length-two paths are natural algebraic incidence statistics. The four distinct poles and minimal recurrence isolate how the central dot-product couples middle vertices and distinguish diamonds from two-level stars. An exact all-q count is a useful classification fact, not a mere routine multiplication identity.

final_claim: For P_m = one minimal point + m antichain points + one maximal point, over every finite field F_q, the ordered one-sided zero-product count in its incidence algebra is an exact sum of four distinct exponentials in m, with minimal order-four recurrence and asymptotic q^3[q^3(3q-2)]^m, including m=0 and characteristic 2.
limitations: Only finite fields, ordered one-sided zero products, ordinal sum singleton/antichain/singleton.
